headline: Charter write-down drives Liberty Broadband to a steep loss
summary_short: Liberty Broadband posted a $2,125M net loss (diluted EPS $(14.86)) in Q2 2026 after a $3.0B other-than-temporary impairment on its Charter equity stake, driven by a sustained decline in Charter's share price. Operating loss narrowed to $4M from $10M a year earlier.
summary_long: Net loss was $2,125M (diluted EPS $(14.86)) versus $383M net income a year ago, driven by a $3.0B other-than-temporary impairment on the Charter equity investment after a sustained Charter share-price decline; share of affiliate losses swung to $(2,653)M from $345M. Operating (G&A) loss narrowed to $4M from $10M on lower professional fees tied to the pending Charter merger. Interest expense fell to $23M on lower rates and April 2026 retirement of the 2053 debentures. Total debt fell to $1,223M from $1,746M at year-end after a new $359M Charter loan and Charter share-repurchase proceeds repaid $617M of margin-loan borrowings. Cash fell to $43M; equity fell to $3,748M, chiefly reflecting the impairment. No company guidance was issued.
